China housing prices still declining
Key Takeaways
In April secondary home transaction prices were down -0.4% MoM (-11.8% YoY)
Notably, secondary home transactions in tier 1 Cities trended up mildly, however the diffusion of the recovery into more Cities is still elusive at this stage
Our China Property team maintains a prudent view and suggests waiting for more evidence of a market recovery to turn constructive.
Exhibit 1: Secondary house prices continue to fall from the peak in June 2021
Source: Centraline, NBS, MS
* Note: For Cities including Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Tianjin, Chengdu. Data up till December

Bottom line: As discussed below, the housing market in China remains weak, deteriorating further YoY in April (albeit at a softer rate), and we think that is likely to remain a concern for investors regarding the European Luxury Goods sector. Secondary home prices and listing volumes witnessed diverging trends among Cities in April amid a pickup in secondary home sales in select top-tier Cities. Our colleagues maintain a prudent view and suggest waiting for more evidence of a market recovery to turn constructive.

What's new? Our HK colleagues published a note last week on the Chinese real estate market (here). Given the importance of Chinese demand for the European Luxury sector (>30% of total spend), and that over 70% of Chinese household wealth lies in real estate, we thought it would be interesting to flag a few data points.
In April, secondary home transaction prices were down -0.4% MoM (-11.8% YoY).

As detailed in our colleague Stephen Cheung's note (here), secondary home prices decline softened slightly in April – falling 0.4% m-m (-11.8% y-y) in the 85 sample Cities they track (vs. -0.6% in March), leading to -1.8% y-y in 4M26. 91% of the

sample Cities recorded m-m decreases, with 19% recording faster declines (vs. 84% in March). However, tier 1 Cities trended up mildly, which the team attributes to their strong secondary home sales that have lasted for longer than expected, especially in Shanghai and Beijing.

Our China Property team stays cautious on the recovery timeline. As per our colleagues, although secondary home sales in select top-tier Cities have exceeded market expectations since March, the diffusion of the recovery into more Cities is still elusive at this stage, in their view. With secondary listing volume and primary inventory staying high, resident sentiment remaining fragile, and rental rates still falling, they expect home sales in these Cities to cool down in coming months amid fading policy impact, though y-y declines may continue to improve on favorable bases.
Primary market home prices dropped -0.2% MoM in March (-3% YoY) vs. -0.8% MoM in February (see note published here) - April data is not yet available.

On the other hand, the equity market remains supportive. The weakness in the housing market has been, over the past 12-18 months, partially offset by the equity market in China. The Shanghai index is now up +25% over the last 12 months, supported by liquidity and policy narratives. To put things in perspective, we estimate that the value destruction in the housing market since December 2024 amounted to approximately RMB 38trn, while the rise in Chinese equity amounted to approximately RMB 31trn over the same period.
